title: "Native Torque Replay"

# Native Torque Replay

## Calculation and Input Meaning

The F06a adapter consumes the authoritative Tools experiment-replay bundle
through `sidekick.lab.mocap`. It drives actual MuJoCo stepping, with the model's
own constraints and contact. The local split lab namespace resolves Tools-owned
subpackages through the central vendor-search helper; the replay schema is
never copied into UD. For each admitted unit-gain hinge motor,
\(p_i=u_i\), and generalized actuator effort is
\(\tau=\sum_i e_{d(i)}u_i\), where \(d(i)\) is the native hinge velocity
index. Native effort is checked against this mapping at every step.

The stored values are post-limit actuator torques in N m. Nonunit gears,
internal actuator dynamics, actuator/joint force clamps, disabled actuator
groups, gravity compensation, plugins, mocap driving and native callbacks
require separate policies and are rejected. Commands outside the native
control range fail instead of being clipped.

## State, Time, and Execution

The complete `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` vector is restored into a fresh plant,
including input and solver warm-start state. Named `qpos` and `qvel` views must
agree with that vector. Their dimensions remain `nq` and `nv`; quaternion
configuration is never flattened into tangent velocity. Translation uses
metres, hinge angles radians, quaternion entries dimensionless, and native
velocity coordinates use metres/second or radians/second as appropriate.
The auxiliary vector uses the installed native state enumeration, with its
provider identity bound to the bundle.

The grid begins at zero and includes every native fixed timestep. Input row
\(u_k\) is held throughout the entire native step, including RK stages.
The final row is an unused explicit sentinel equal to the preceding input.
The adapter records the solver, integrator, timestep, initialization and
input-player policy. Native automatic resetting is disabled; a failed or
nonfinite trajectory raises an error. Initial external applied forces are
forbidden. No feedback law, reference trajectory or observation callback is
accepted by the replay interface.

## Identity and Preconditions

Tools validates canonical bundle integrity. Replay also compares actual
source XML, compiled MJB, loaded native function-module and adapter digests,
ordered channels, complete initial state and executed policy. The fresh
execution model is checked again after validation, closing model replacement
between those phases. Compiled identity captures included model resources;
this is not a complete operating-system or transitive-library attestation.
Run in an exclusively owned process: process-global callbacks must not be
mutated concurrently. A subprocess sandbox is not implemented by this slice.

## Evidence and Remaining Qualification

The synthetic floating-root fixture has `nq != nv`, a hinge motor and a
bounded reference controller. Independent replay of its saved held torque
matches native controlled positions within absolute tolerance `1e-12`.
Tests verify saturation occurred before export, exact restoration of nonzero
warm-start state, callback refusal without evaluation, malformed state,
quaternion, bounds, grid, transmission and model replacement rejection.
These are deterministic same-provider replay checks, not a measured-error
tolerance or proof of numerical convergence.

F06a does not close six-engine parity or certify anatomy, contact/grip,
full-horizon capture agreement, muscle recruitment or robustness. F06 and
F07/F08 retain those gates. The first local run imports the pending Tools
T01 branch explicitly; consumer acceptance requires its merged pinned commit.
See `docs/development/feedback_controls/F06_NATIVE_TORQUE_TURNOVER.md` for
executed commands and dependency status.
